reason: The winding drum needs a crank to wind the lifting cord, and the ratchet should help hold the load.
expectation: The crank and ratchet will attach to the winding drum.

effect: The crank and drum form a hand winch, ready to install on the crane.
reaction: The trade-off between turning effect and hand travel is a useful detail.
reason: The winch needs to be mounted on the crane before it can lift a load.
expectation: The winch will attach to the crane frame.

effect: The winch is mounted on the crane; it now needs a lifting connection.
reaction: The assembly is progressing as expected.
reason: The lifting cord should connect the winch and pulley to a load.
expectation: The cord and hook will be fitted to the crane.

effect: The crane now has a lifting line and hook, but still needs a way to hold a raised load.
reason: The pawl should engage the ratchet to keep the winch from unwinding under load.
expectation: The pawl and release lever will attach to the winch.

effect: The pawl cannot be fitted yet, so I need to find what the crane requires first.
reaction: That was unexpected; the holding mechanism seemed like a natural next step.
reason: The padded test weight looks appropriate for checking the lifting line before using the basket.
expectation: The crane will lift the test weight and reveal whether it is stable.

alternatives.reason: Checking its available partners could clarify the required sequence.

effect: The low test showed that the stiff frame can still tip, so it needs more stability before lifting the basket.
reaction: The distinction between bending and tipping is useful and a little surprising.
reason: The rear ballast should counterbalance the load and keep the back feet down.

choice.with: Crane lifting at its back feet

expectation: The ballast will stabilize the crane for another lift.

effect: The ballast keeps the crane's feet down during the low test, so I can try fitting the holding mechanism now.
reaction: The repeated test makes the ballast's purpose clear.
reason: The pawl should engage the ratchet to hold a raised load, and it may now be available after the stability test.
expectation: The pawl and release lever will attach to the winch so the load can be held and released.

effect: The pawl now holds the drum against unwinding, with a controlled release for lowering.
reaction: The explanation makes the ratchet and release sequence clear.
reason: The basket is the remaining load to lift, hold, and lower with the completed mechanism.
expectation: The crane will lift the basket, hold it with the pawl, and lower it gently.

effect: The basket test confirmed that the pawl holds the load and the lever allows controlled lowering; the crane goal is complete.
reaction: Seeing the assembled mechanism make a delivery was a satisfying payoff.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the crane with the padded weight was most worthwhile: it showed that a stiff frame can still tip, giving the ballast a clear purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: The unsuccessful attempt to fit the pawl was the least worthwhile moment; the result did not explain why it could not be fitted yet.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the crane's back feet lifted even though its braced frame remained stiff.

arbitrary.text: The pawl's initial unavailability felt somewhat arbitrary because its connection to the ratchet seemed plausible before the stability test.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: testing a construction, diagnosing its tipping, and seeing the holding mechanism work made the mechanisms worth exploring.
